lesson.title: Doing it again

steps.headline: A while loop repeats its body for as long as its condition is true.

lead.text: Eating sweets was a loop: the same action, again and again. A while loop checks its condition before every pass. If it is true, the indented body runs once more. If it is false, the loop ends.
Each run of the body is one iteration.
Count passes, not checks. The condition is checked before each pass, and once more at the end, when it fails.

reveal.text: The body ran for x = 3, 2 and 1, then x = 0 failed the check. Four checks, three passes.

steps.headline: Trace x = 10, then while x > 4: x = x - 3. When does it stop?

workedSteps.text: Check 7 > 4: true. Run the body again.
The body ran twice and x finished at 4.

steps.headline: Trace x = 0, then while x > 0: x = x - 1. How many times does the body run?

workedSteps.text: Check the condition before anything else.
Count the passes of the body.

steps.headline: A for loop runs its body once for each value a range gives it.

lead.text: range(4) gives the values 0, 1, 2 and 3. It stops before 4. A for loop runs its body once for each value, so you can count the passes from the range alone.
The loop variable i takes each value in turn. The body here does not use i. It only adds to x.

reveal.text: The body ran once for each value in the range: four times, adding 2 each time, so x grew by 8.

lead.text: A loop only ends if its body moves the tested value towards making the condition false. This one starts at 3 and tests x > 0, but its body adds 1.

reveal.text: Each pass moved x closer to the value where x > 0 fails. A body that moves away from the stopping point never stops.

lesson.orientation: Count how many times a loop runs, and see what makes it stop.
lesson.nextAction: Count the checks a linear search makes in the best and worst cases.

blocks.text: A bag holds 7 sweets. You eat 2 at a time, and you keep going only while 2 or more are left.

intro.promise: By the end you'll count how many times a loop body runs, and spot the change that would stop a loop from ending.

recap.keyIdea: A loop checks its condition before every pass and stops when it is false. Its body has to move towards that, or the loop never stops.

blocks.text: You counted three passes as x fell from 3 to 0, and no passes when the first check failed. You saw range(4) take x from 1 to 9.

recap.nextHook: You can now repeat steps. Next: a loop that looks through a list for one item.

questions.prompt: How many times does the body run?
hints: Check x > 0 before every pass.
List the values of x at which the body starts, beginning with the initial value in the code.
Do not count the final failed condition as a body execution.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The body runs for starting values 3, 2 and 1: three passes.

questions.onCorrect: 3. The body runs once for each check that passes. The check that fails ends the loop without a pass.

misconceptions.feedback: That counts the check that failed. A failed check does not run the body.
The body also runs when x is 1. List the value of x at the start of each pass.

questions.prompt: How many times does this body run?
hints: A while loop tests its condition before its first pass.
Compare the initial value with the strict condition before changing it.
If that first test fails, no body instruction runs.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The first test 0 > 0 is false, so the body runs zero times.

questions.onCorrect: 0. The check comes first, so a loop whose condition starts false never runs its body.

misconceptions.feedback: The body only runs after a passing check, and the first check fails.

questions.prompt: What is x at the end?
hints: The for loop repeats the addition four times.
Each pass adds 2 to the current x, starting from 1.
Add the total increase to the initial value.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Four additions of 2 take x from 1 to 1 + 8 = 9.

questions.onCorrect: 9. A for loop counts its own passes. Four values in the range means four additions of 2.

misconceptions.feedback: That adds 2 only three times. Count the values range(4) gives.
That counts five passes. The range stops before 4, so it gives four values.
That is x after one pass. The body runs once for every value in the range.

questions.prompt: Change the body to subtract 1. When the repaired loop ends, what is x?
hints: Trace the repaired subtraction from the given starting value.
The loop continues only while x is positive.
Stop at the first value that makes the displayed loop condition false.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The repaired body visits 2, 1 and 0, then the condition is false.

questions.onCorrect: 0. The repaired body moves x towards the failing check, so the loop ends the moment x stops being positive.

misconceptions.feedback: At that value the condition is still true, so the body runs again.
The check comes before the body. Once the condition fails, the body does not run again.

questions.prompt: Start x = 2. Repeat x = x * 2 three times. What is final x?
hints: Apply each doubling to the result of the previous doubling.
The first pass changes 2 to 4.
Perform exactly two more doublings.
questions.onCorrect: 16. Each pass works on the last result: 4, then 8, then 16.

misconceptions.feedback: That multiplies 2 by 3 once. Each pass doubles the result of the last one.
That is two doublings. The loop runs three times.

questions.prompt: Which change lets “while x > 0” stop from x = 5?
hints: The loop stops only when its condition becomes false.
Choose an update that moves a positive x toward zero.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Subtracting 1 from each positive x eventually reaches zero, where x > 0 is false. An update that increases x moves away from the stopping condition.

questions.onCorrect: Subtracting 1 moves x towards 0, where x > 0 fails. A body must move towards the stopping condition.

misconceptions.feedback: Adding 1 moves x further from the stopping point, so the condition stays true.
If x never changes, neither does the check, so the loop never ends.

questions.prompt: How many times do you eat?
hints: How many sweets are left after the first time?
Keep going until fewer than two sweets are left.
Count the times you ate, not the sweets.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The bag goes 7, 5, 3, 1 sweets. You eat when 2 or more are left, which happens three times.

questions.onCorrect: 3. You repeated one action and checked the rule before each go. That is what a loop does.

misconceptions.feedback: You cannot eat two from a single sweet. The rule only lets you eat while two or more are left.

questions.prompt: Why does the loop stop when x reaches 4?
hints: What does the loop do before each pass?

acceptedIdeas: 4 > 4 is false, so the body is not run again.
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: 4 > 4 is false, so the body is not run again.

choices.label: 4 > 4 is false, so the body is not run again.
Loops always stop after two passes.
x can never be smaller than 4.

questions.onCorrect: The condition is checked before every pass. When it comes out false, the body is not run again.

misconceptions.feedback: Nothing limits a loop to two passes. The condition alone decides.
x would go lower if the body ran again. The check before each pass is what stops it.

questions.prompt: When does a while loop check its condition?
hints: Does the check come before the body or after it?

choices.label: Only after the body has run.
Once, at the start of the program.

questions.onCorrect: The check comes before each pass, so the loop can end as soon as the condition is false.

misconceptions.feedback: Then the body would run once even when the condition is false from the start.
It checks on every pass. Otherwise a loop could never stop.

questions.prompt: How many times does a for loop over range(3) run its body?
hints: List the values range(3) gives, starting at 0.
questions.onCorrect: The body runs once for each value the range gives, and the range stops before its limit.

misconceptions.feedback: Count every value range(3) gives, including 0.
range(3) stops before 3, so 3 is not one of its values.

questions.prompt: Start x = 19. While x > 6, subtract 5 from x. What is x when the loop ends?
hints: List the value of x after each pass.
Check the condition before each pass, not after.
Stop at the first value that fails the check.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: 19 → 14 → 9 → 4. The check 4 > 6 fails, so the loop ends with x = 4.

questions.onCorrect: 4. The loop kept running while the check passed, and ended on the first value that failed it.

misconceptions.feedback: The check 9 > 6 is still true, so the body runs again.
The check before the last pass fails first, so that pass never happens.
